rules.description: Opening metadata uses the required standard keys in their defined order.
Opening metadata keys must not be duplicated.
Every document-set file ends with the required identity trailer.
Root short identity handles derive from the first 128 bits of their full digests.
The root set_digest matches byte-exact recomputation across the complete document set.
A document-set root is closed to unrelated files, symbolic links, invalid UTF-8, and empty directories.
Every file in a document set declares the same DocAI Messaging version.
Every file in a document set declares the same output profile.
Every file in a document set declares the same exact perspective.
Every file in a document set carries the same set_id.
Every file in a document set carries the same projection_id.
A direct Sources catalog uses its required columns and contains at least one structurally valid authoritative-input row.
Source IDs use the fixed grammar, exclude the reserved all value, and are globally unique in ASCII lexical order.
Unknown API identity or contract version cells have source-qualified localized markers and propagate requires-input knowledge.
A sha256 source Revision contains exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; none remains valid when no stable revision exists.
source_refs is all or a unique ASCII-ordered canonical ID list that resolves within the Sources catalog and covers each source shard's own rows.
Source Shards routes to unique source-index files whose structure, inclusive bounds, Kinds, and non-empty rows match the root route.
Fixed-point source resolution loads every matching and transitive shard, terminates contributor cycles, and finds each requested ID exactly once.
The root INDEX uses the fixed title and ordered Sources, operation-routing, Workflows, and optional Unprojected Operations sections.
A root INDEX uses the profile-specific optional or required profile-link label and relative-directory grammar.
Flat and sharded Operations content uses non-empty channel-file subsections with canonical operation-table columns and unique existing channel paths.
Operation routing rows use valid actions, channels, set-unique operation names, canonical primary and reply message routing, task labels, and informative summaries.
Required and supplemental context lists use canonical unique paths, preserve the none sentinel distinction, target eligible existing files, and never overlap.
Operation Shards routes to unique non-empty operation-index files whose structure, Tasks, Actions, and inclusive routing bounds match their actual rows.

Simulated exact retrieval records every matching and false-positive shard, semantic uncertainty loads all shards, and source provenance comes from selected contract files rather than aggregate operation-index scope.

rules.readme_section: §3.2 INDEX.md(required) / §3.6 Source Integration and Publication Safety
rules.description: Direct Unprojected Operations use source-resolving UTF-8 byte-length-prefixed grouping keys, at most one marker per completeness dimension, root completeness aggregation, and source-aware non-disclosure or generation-failure expectations.
Unprojected Operation Shards routes to unique non-empty index files whose fixed structure, Source refs, marker completeness, and grouping-key ownership match their actual markers.
Unprojected-operation exact retrieval loads every shard listing the selected source ID, while semantic uncertainty loads every unprojected-operation shard.
CONVENTIONS.md uses its required title and every fixed convention heading exactly once in canonical order without title-level prose.

rules.readme_section: §3.3 CONVENTIONS.md(required) / §3.4 Output Profiles and Incomplete Information
rules.description: Every convention section contains exactly one canonical none, whole-section unknown, replacement unsupported, or non-empty expanded core state with required marker adjacency.

rules.readme_section: §3.3 CONVENTIONS.md(required) / §3.6 Authoritative Input Resolution and Schema Representability
rules.description: Format and format_annotation fragments resolve exactly once through a unique ordered Data Representation format catalog, and affected operations retain that convention in their dependency closure.

rules.readme_section: §3.3 CONVENTIONS.md / §3.4 Output Profiles and Incomplete Information
rules.description: Error Handling defines each valid common failure-signal shape exactly once as a receive-side expanded block or an exact whole-shape replacement.
Each routed channel file contains exactly its routed operation definitions, without a file-level wrapper, and every operation uses the fixed required section order.
Each operation heading matches its routed action, channel, and set-unique name and is followed by canonical purpose and deprecation placement.
Behavior contains the six canonical non-empty keys in order, uses post-key markers for unknown facts, and states delivery with a valid qualified guarantee.
Operation Bindings and Channel Parameters and Bindings use canonical states, tables and post-table markers, subsection order, leading-empty collapse, and exact address-parameter coverage.
Primary and reply header and payload-field tables use direction-correct Required or Presence columns and values, valid Nullable values and unknown markers, and direction-correct root-row invariants.
Expanded Messages contain Headers, Bindings, and non-collapsed Payload in order, with canonical subsection states and only leading empty Headers or Bindings eligible for collapse.

rules.readme_section: §3.4 Output Profiles and Incomplete Information / §4.1 Section Rules — Message sections
rules.description: Message names are valid, operation-unique, routed and lexically ordered; multi-message selections are observable one- or two-sentence rules; complete replacements retain only required routing prose and the exact matching marker.

rules.readme_section: §3.4 Output Profiles and Incomplete Information / §4.1 Section Rules — Message Payload
rules.description: Payloads use their direction-correct whole state, canonical representation boundaries, media types, nullability, unknown or replacement forms, adapter-correct examples, or opaque raw-binary prose in fixed order.

rules.readme_section: §3.5 Canonical Syntax and Boundaries / §3.6 Schema Representability / §4.1 Section Rules — Message Payload
rules.description: Payload field tables use valid paths, types, object openness and canonically ordered constraints and cover every represented example field with exact JSON parsing.
Concrete media types are unique with explicit sender selection and receiver branching for alternatives, while tagged and untagged variants are complete, canonical, ordered and exactly discriminated.

rules.readme_section: §3.4 Output Profiles and Incomplete Information / §4.1 Section Rules — Reply
rules.description: Reply contains canonically ordered leading deviations followed by exactly one none, whole-section unknown, replacement unsupported, or expanded core state.
Expanded Reply uses canonical channel, correlation, and timeout keys plus a static or dynamic addressed Channel with exact Parameters and scoped Bindings.
Only expanded Reply contributes an exact lexically ordered reply Message set to its containing operation's INDEX routing, with complete observable selection and no synthesized operation.
Failure Handling contains canonically ordered leading deviations followed by exactly one none, whole-section unknown, replacement unsupported, or expanded table state.
Expanded Failure Handling uses the canonical non-empty table and exact common or inline Signal references that resolve once, with inline shapes in first-use order.

rules.readme_section: §3.4 Output Profiles and Incomplete Information / §4.1 Section Rules — Failure Handling
rules.description: Inline failure shapes have valid labels and use the shared receive-side Headers, Bindings, and non-collapsed Payload grammar or an exact whole-shape replacement.

rules.readme_section: §3.4 Output Profiles and Incomplete Information / §3.6 Authoritative Input Resolution and Schema Representability
rules.description: Authoritative inputs distinguish known absence, missing knowledge, known unrepresentability, and unresolved equal-priority conflicts as none, unknown, unsupported, and generation failure respectively.

rules.readme_section: §3 Opening Metadata / §3.4 Output Profiles and Incomplete Information
rules.description: Each file's coverage and knowledge exactly match its unsupported and unknown markers, and root INDEX aggregates those states across the whole set without inventing incompleteness.

rules.readme_section: §3 Contract Completeness and Implementation Readiness / §6.1 Recommended Retrieval Recipe
rules.description: Selected-operation readiness is blocked only by unknown or unsupported facts in the selected operation's required retrieval scope, not by markers confined to unrelated units.
Markdown headings and backtick-fenced blocks retain deterministic source-line boundaries.
Pipe tables use source-level boundary pipes, escape parity, separators, and consistent column counts.
Docs-root-relative paths and INDEX profile links use their exact ASCII source grammars.
Required one-line prose uses the literal source-level sentence-terminator grammar.
